sections.h2: What can the Bay County Register of Deeds office do for a seller?
sections.html:
Think of this office as the county's land filing cabinet. Deeds, mortgages, notices of pending suits and certified copies all land here to be indexed, and the resulting public record is what every title company reads before a Bay County closing.

The counter opens Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. through 5:00 p.m. Hands on research with staff wraps up a half hour sooner, and nobody locks the door at midday. Beginning January 1, 2018, each instrument receives a single Document Number in place of the old Liber and Page pair.

The office page also gathers links that sellers and heirs find handy, including a Bay County cemetery directory, contact details for local city and township officials, and state forms from Michigan.gov. Tax certifications carry their own $5 charge, paid to the Treasurer.

  • Doxpop offers search any hour of the day. Its help line, 1-866-369-7671, assists with account sign up.
  • Doxpop Property Watch emails you free of charge whenever someone attempts to transfer title to your land.
  • Approved eRecording partners are listed on the office page for electronic delivery.
  • A package sent by USPS, UPS or FedEx should include postage paid return packaging addressed to you.

sections.h2: What will recording a deed in Bay County set me back?
sections.html:
Bay County's statutory fee schedule sets a single price, $30.00 per document, for a deed, mortgage, lis pendens or any similar instrument. Out of each $30, four dollars move on to the state's survey and remonumentation program. Liens held by the state or federal government, fixture filings, plats, state deeds and tax reversion papers are not charged that four dollar share.

The certificate comes from MCL 211.135 and covers deeds with a warranty clause, land contracts, land contract assignments that carry a warranty, and condominium master deeds.

sections.h2: Why might Bay County reject my deed?
sections.html:
The office publishes sixteen rules taken from Michigan recording statutes. If a paper fails any of them it is sent back, and several lost days can upset a closing schedule. These are the flaws that catch sellers most.

  • Signatures must be live originals, with each signer's name typed or printed beneath the line and matching the notary's certificate exactly.
  • A deed has to give the grantee's street or post office address, and it also needs the name and address of the person who prepared it.
  • Any paper that conveys or burdens land needs an acknowledgment from a Michigan notary, judge or court clerk.
  • Page one needs a 2.5 inch empty band along the top, with half an inch of margin on all remaining sides. Print in black ink, 10 point or bigger, on white paper.
  • Paper size runs from 8.5 by 11 up to 8.5 by 14 inches, and the first line should say what kind of instrument it is.
  • If a deed refers to a surviving owner, pair it with a certified death certificate unless one is already of record.
  • A court order must be certified and sealed by the clerk, and any Social Security number has to have its first five digits removed.

One more rule on the list asks conveyances to give the marital status of male grantors, citing MCLA 565.221.

sections.h2: What is the transfer tax math for a Bay County sale?
sections.html:
Two levies arise at recording, one county (MCL 207.505) and one state (MCL 207.526). Either the deed states the total price on its front, or the filer hands in a Real Estate Transfer Affidavit with that number. Both taxes are due unless an exemption applies, and the instrument itself has to claim it.

Try a house priced at the Census median of $152,200. At $7.50 per thousand, the state share lands near $1,141. At $1.10 per thousand, the county share is near $167. The recorder would collect about $1,309 in all.

The two exemption lists overlap but are not identical. Each excludes consideration below $100, security instruments, leases, court orders that set no price, land contracts whose title has not passed, and foreclosure transfers involving government backed loans. Only the state act goes on to name gifts from a parent or grandparent to a child or grandchild. Ask the title agent or the office which section covers your paper.

sections.h2: Which state fee rules stand behind the Bay County schedule?
sections.html:
The Revised Judicature Act, at MCL 600.2567, governs what a register may charge, and the Bay County page cites it. The statute also prices the services that sellers and heirs request most often.

  • Copies run $1.00 per page. Certifying a recorded paper adds $5.00.
  • Index searches by grantor and grantee cost 50 cents per year covered, with a $5.00 minimum.
  • Filing a miscellaneous paper costs $1.00.
  • Fees are paid on delivery of the paper, with exceptions for electronic filers and for government filers that have a payment agreement.

A charter county can pass its own schedule by ordinance, so confirm any copy or search fee with Bay County staff before you write a check.

sections.h2: In what order should a seller handle recording in Bay County?
sections.html:
Work in this order and you save a trip. Settle who must sign and whether a survivor appears on the deed, so the death certificate is on hand. If the deed has a warranty clause, request the tax certificate from the County Treasurer. Have the deed drafted with the full price written in, or complete the transfer affidavit. Have it notarized in Michigan, then hand the original to the title agent or post it with a return envelope.

Once the paper is recorded, you receive a Document Number, which is how the instrument turns up in the online index. File it with your closing papers. Anyone who holds other land in the county should also enroll in Property Watch.

When a paper bounces, the cause usually sits on the sixteen item list: a mismatched name, a narrow margin, an unsealed court order or an exposed Social Security number. Correct that single defect and resubmit instead of redrafting everything.

sections.h2: Which other Bay County offices does a deed touch?
sections.html:
A sale crosses several counters. The Treasurer, upstairs at 515 Center Ave., writes the tax certificate and collects late tax. Equalization answers parcel and description questions. The assessor in your city or township keeps the value record, while the Register preserves the chain of title.

Bay County borders Saginaw Bay and counts 14 townships and 4 cities. Census figures for 2020 to 2024 show a median owned home worth $152,200, 77.0 percent owner occupancy, 45,103 households and a median household income of $61,763. New construction is slight: 67 building permits were counted for 2025.

faqs.q: What does a Bay County recording cost?
faqs.a: It is $30.00 per document, with $4.00 of the total sent to the state survey fund. A paper that assigns or discharges multiple instruments adds $3.00 for each additional one.

faqs.q: Are Bay County land records searchable on the web?
faqs.a: Yes. Doxpop offers searching at any hour, and the office suggests its free Property Watch alert so you learn of any attempt to move your title.

faqs.q: Is eRecording available in Bay County?
faqs.a: It is. The office page names the approved partners that deliver title documents electronically to the county.

faqs.q: What does the Bay County tax certificate cost on a warranty deed?
faqs.a: Five dollars, on its own check, payable to the Bay County Treasurer instead of the Register.

faqs.q: What transfer tax rates does Bay County list?
faqs.a: The Register shows $7.50 per $1,000 of consideration for the state and $1.10 per $1,000 for the county. An exempt transfer must say why on the instrument.
